Both are the only `*AgentTest.java` files in the project, and all 50 test methods pass.

I created two self-contained JUnit 5 test classes:
- `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/StringUtilsAgentTest.java` — covers empty/blank checks, trim/strip, equals, contains, startsWith/endsWith, indexOf, substring boundary cases, split/join, replace/remove, repeat/pad/center, case conversion, reverse, numeric/alpha checks, defaults, abbreviate/truncate, wrap/unwrap, chomp/chop, compare/difference, left/right/mid, Levenshtein distance, normalize/delete whitespace, overlay/rotate, code points, and constants.
- `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/StrBuilderAgentTest.java` — covers constructors (including negative/zero capacity), append variants, chained calls, boundary exceptions for `charAt`/`deleteCharAt`/`delete`/`insert`/`setCharAt`/`setLength`, delete/insert/replace operations, indexOf/lastIndexOf, contains/startsWith/endsWith, equals/hashCode, substring/mid/left/right strings, clear/size/isEmpty, reverse, trim, appendSeparator, padding, char array access, capacity management, subSequence, build/toString consistency, and null/newline text handling.

Both files kept to Java 8 syntax (no lambdas — `assertThrows` uses anonymous `Executable` implementations — no diamond operator, no underscores in literals) and are fully self-contained with no dependency on other test classes.
